question: For $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix},\quad C=\begin{bmatrix}1 & k \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix},$$ suppose both $B$ and $C$ are inverses of $A$. Determine $k$ and hence verify that the two inverses are identical.
explanation:
Condition for $C$ to be an inverse
$$AC=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & k \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & k+1 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
Since $C$ is an inverse of $A$, $AC=I$. Therefore, $$k+1=0\Rightarrow k=-1$$
Comparison with $B$
Substituting $k=-1$, $$C=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}=B$$
Uniqueness verification
Thus, the two matrices claimed to be inverses are identical, in agreement with the uniqueness of the inverse.
